specification.problem: Learn a hidden n-bit parity s from a quantum example oracle that prepares 2^{-n/2} sum_x |x>|s.x mod 2>, possibly followed by depolarizing noise on its output qubits. Use Hadamard (Bernstein-Vazirani) Fourier sampling on each noisy copy, then bitwise majority vote over m=O(log n/(1-2p')^2) runs.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: n=3 or 4 data qubits plus 1 label qubit, one oracle query per run, H on all qubits, measure the data qubits, then classical majority voting across runs. Noise is modeled as per-qubit depolarizing noise after the oracle, and the sketch's single-qubit Pauli analysis is taken as given. Outside scope: any proof of the query or computational complexity bounds, exact optimality, the LPN hardness argument, and the quantum-classical separation claim. Noise-rate estimation is also out of scope.

equations.label: Quantum example state
equations.description: The noiseless coherent example oracle applied to |0^n>|0>, with the label qubit carrying f_s(x).
equations.abstract_quote: making queries to a quantum example oracle
equations.justification: The abstract names a quantum example oracle for parities. The coherent uniform-superposition form is the standard definition, and the task sketch states it.

equations.label: Fourier sampling
equations.description: After the oracle, H on the label gives |-> by phase kickback, and the data register is the state 2^{-n/2} sum_x (-1)^{s.x}|x>. H^{\otimes n} then maps the data register to |s>. Equivalently, the state before the final label H is |s>|->.
equations.justification: Standard Bernstein-Vazirani identity: 2^{-n/2} sum_x |x>|s.x> = 2^{-n/2} sum_x (-1)^{s.x}|x>|-> after label basis change.

equations.label: Effective noisy readout
equations.description: Depolarizing noise after the oracle becomes independent bit-flip noise on the Fourier-sampled string. X or Y errors flip the readout bit, and the label qubit's Z errors do not affect it.
equations.justification: Taken from the task sketch, which assumes independent depolarizing noise on each output qubit after the oracle. The abstract only says that noise at any constant rate keeps learning efficient. Exact independence and the Z-error argument are not checked here.
assumptions: Per-qubit depolarizing channel with a uniform random Pauli with probability p
Independent errors across qubits and runs

equations.label: Majority vote
equations.description: Bitwise majority vote across the m runs recovers each bit of s.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes majority voting. The abstract only asserts efficiency of noisy quantum learning, with at most logarithmic overhead.
assumptions: m odd or ties broken arbitrarily

equations.label: Repetition count
equations.description: A Chernoff/Hoeffding bound per bit, followed by a union bound over n bits, gives total error probability at most n e^{-m(1-2p')^2/2}, which is 1/poly(n) for m=O(log n/(1-2p')^2).
equations.abstract_quote: does not increase the computational (or query) complexity of quantum learning more than logarithmically
equations.justification: The logarithmic overhead is consistent with this bound. The exact constants come from standard Hoeffding and are not from the abstract.

registers.name: data
registers.role: Oracle input/output register holding x, read as s after H^{\otimes n}; qubit i corresponds to s_i

registers.name: label
registers.role: Carries f_s(x); H is applied to it to produce |->

specification.initial_state: |0^n>|0>, with the oracle placeholder acting on all n+1 qubits to produce the example state

steps.description: Place the example-oracle black box once on data+label, starting from |0^n>|0>. If noise is simulated, apply a depolarizing channel to each qubit after the oracle by sampling Pauli errors with probability p.
Apply H to the label qubit, then H to every data qubit.
Measure the n data qubits only. Read bit i as bits[::-1][i], which is s_i for little-endian Qiskit order. Repeat the whole circuit m times with one query each.
Classically take the bitwise majority across the m strings to output the estimate of s.

specification.measurement: Measure the n data qubits in the computational basis after the Hadamards. The label qubit is not needed; measure it only if the task requires.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Per-bit majority vote over m measured strings, with qubit index i mapped via bits[::-1][i].
assumptions: Chosen instance: n=3 or 4, one query per run, m set from the target error rate
Oracle is the standard coherent example oracle with no offset
Depolarizing noise is per-qubit, independent, after the oracle, and uses p<3/4
The noisy oracle is supplied by the task, or noise is simulated by sampling Paulis
The noise rate is known, or at least bounded away from the 1/2 threshold on p'
missing_information: Exact noise model used by the paper's analysis (the sketch's p'=2p/3 effective flip rate is not given in the abstract)
Whether the actual method uses Fourier sampling plus majority vote, or a different or more noise-robust procedure
Whether the task's black box includes noise or the runner adds it
Details of the label-qubit Z-error argument
